current.text: LeBron James left the Lakers for the Sixers. Reaves re-signed with the Lakers for 4 years and 185 million. He and Luka Doncic are the remaining core.
He is a projected starter next to Doncic, Grimes, Thybulle and Kessler.
With LeBron gone, experts expect his usage to rise, his assist rate most of all. They project about 28% usage and 36 minutes.

Experts see a floor around picks 15 to 18 and first-round upside. With 30% usage and 7.5 assists he could be a first-round player. The newest advice is to take him at the end of round 2, not in round 1.
Experts disagree on a top-12 finish. Dan picks Reaves over Jamal Murray and Donovan Mitchell as most likely to finish top 12. Josh says it is probably Murray.
His ESPN rank (50, later 64) is far too low. He is the best target on the Lakers, especially on ESPN.
His Yahoo rank of about 20 is good value in category leagues.
In an auction mock Josh valued him at about 36 USD and called his 40 USD price an overpay.
His efficiency could fall this season. It already dipped toward the end of last season.
If Doncic misses time, Reaves would run around 32% usage and works as a first-round replacement.
Andy expects heavy scrutiny after his new contract. If the team is not working, Reaves could be the player the Lakers trade, even if he is playing well.
Josh says he could have been an All-Star last season if he had not been injured.
The Lakers have the second most back-to-backs in the league. Their playoff schedule with a March 28 end is 3-4-3, in the bottom half of the league.

durable.text: He takes many free throws at a great percentage and adds points, assists and threes.
Turnovers are his weak category, and experts say he lacks defensive stats.
Experts disagree on his field goal efficiency. One calls it excellent. Another says it can be a problem, and Josh expects a worse FG% than Jamal Murray's.
He played like a second-round player when he shared the floor with only one of LeBron or Doncic. He fell to third option when he played with both.
Andy sees his game as very similar to Doncic's and thinks he brings little that Doncic does not.
He has had groin problems, so soft tissue injuries are a risk.
He is a better category league player than points league player.

note: Yahoo values him at 33 USD (average cost 31.7 USD) and ESPN at only 15 USD. He went for 25 USD in our league last season, and Josh puts him at about 36 USD, so 30 to 36 USD is a fair price. Paying 40 USD is an overpay. He is a strong FT%, points, assists and threes piece that fits punt TO builds best. Early in the season, check that his usage climbs toward 28% without LeBron and whether his FG% holds near last season's 49%.
